The identity element folds into a normal call like any other argument
sage.note: compute-engine folds the inner Min() into its identity element +Infinity before combining with 5; Sage's inner min() has no identity for zero arguments and raises before the fold can happen.
julia.note: Julia raises an error for this argument (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty collection i), where compute-engine and Wolfram answer or extend Min to it.

caption: Nested lists are flattened into the pool
The numeric arguments collapse to their minimum; symbolic ones stay
The min of two [[Interval]]s is the interval of possible minima, $[-3, 3]$
wolfram.note: compute-engine's Min of two intervals returns the interval-valued min [-3, 3]; Wolfram collapses to the scalar lower bound -3 since Interval[1,3] is entirely dominated by Interval[-3,5].
sympy.note: SymPy leaves Min(...) over an AccumBounds unevaluated; ours computes the image.

Multiple arguments -- lists included -- are flattened into one pool rather than compared list-by-list. See [[Max]]
rust.note: The mapping takes two scalars; compute-engine's Min is variadic and flattens its list operands.

caption: With no arguments it returns the identity element $+\infty$ (Max, whose identity is $-\infty$, still returns NaN)
sage.note: compute-engine's Min() answers its identity element +Infinity, per Wolfram's convention; Sage's builtin min() has no identity for zero arguments and raises ValueError.
julia.note: Julia raises an error for this argument (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty collection i), where compute-engine and Wolfram answer or extend Min to it.

caption: The min of an empty list is NaN
wolfram.note: compute-engine answers NaN for Min of an empty list; Wolfram defines Min[{}] as +Infinity, the identity element for Min.
sage.note: Both decline on an empty collection: compute-engine answers NaN for Min([]), and Sage's min() raises ValueError: min() iterable argument is empty.
sympy.note: compute-engine gives NaN for the min of an empty list; SymPy's Min() is the identity ∞.
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers NaN, Julia raises an error (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty co).

caption: ComplexInfinity is unordered, so Min cannot compare it: the call stays unevaluated, as in Wolfram
sage.note: Sage orders unsigned infinity against 1 and answers 1; Wolfram and compute-engine leave Min(~oo, 1) unevaluated, and SymPy raises, since ~oo is not comparable.
sympy.note: compute-engine leaves the call unevaluated; SymPy raises, since zoo is not comparable.

caption: The empty [[Finset]] answers as an empty list does: NaN
wolfram.note: compute-engine answers NaN for the min of an empty list; Wolfram defines Min[{}] as +Infinity.
sage.note: Python's min of an empty list raises; compute-engine answers NaN.
sympy.note: compute-engine answers NaN for the min of an empty list; SymPy's Min() is oo, the identity element.
julia.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers NaN, Julia raises an error (ArgumentError: reducing over an empty co).
